evals.name: natural-language-research
evals.prompt: Use Synthetic search to find out how people handle cancellation safety with tokio::select!, and summarise the main approaches with sources.
evals.expected_output: Checks SYNTHETIC_API_KEY without printing it, runs one or more focused queries with node scripts/search.js --compact --save, reads highlights first, opens full text from the saved file only when needed, discards irrelevant results, and answers with cited URLs.

assertions.text: Uses scripts/search.js --compact (or an equivalent highlights-only projection) rather than dumping raw JSON into context
Cites the result URLs used in the answer
Does not switch to a different search provider when Synthetic was requested

evals.name: site-restriction-uses-operators
evals.prompt: Search Synthetic for tokio select cancellation, but only from docs.rs and GitHub.
evals.expected_output: Puts site:docs.rs site:github.com in the query string (or uses --site twice), and explains that body parameters such as includeDomains are silently ignored.

assertions.text: Restricts with site: operators in the query or the helper's --site flag
Does not rely on includeDomains or another body parameter

evals.name: more-results-than-five
evals.prompt: Use Synthetic search and give me 20 results about Bun vs Deno startup performance.
evals.expected_output: Explains each search returns exactly 5 results and numResults-style parameters are ignored, then runs several distinct focused queries (in parallel), merges them by URL, and checks quota first if the batch is large.

assertions.text: States that the API returns a fixed 5 results per search
Achieves breadth with multiple distinct queries rather than a count parameter

evals.name: long-query-truncation
evals.prompt: Paste this entire 9,000-character stack trace into a Synthetic search and add site:github.com at the end.
evals.expected_output: Explains that only the first 4,096 characters are searched, so the trailing site: filter would be dropped; extracts the distinctive error line and keeps the operator inside the limit.

assertions.text: Mentions the 4,096-character effective query limit
Shortens the query to the distinctive error text instead of sending the full trace

evals.name: quota-check
evals.prompt: How many Synthetic searches do I have left this hour, and do searches eat into my model credits?
evals.expected_output: Runs node scripts/search.js quotas or GET /v2/quotas (free), reads search.hourly.requests/limit/renewsAt, and explains searches only consume the hourly search bucket, not subscription requests or weekly credits.

assertions.text: Uses /v2/quotas or the helper's quotas command and notes it is free
Explains searches count only against search.hourly

evals.name: published-optional
evals.prompt: The Synthetic docs show a published date, but most of my results don't have one. Which should I trust?
evals.expected_output: Explains published is optional and present on a minority of results, recommends treating it as optional and not inferring recency from rank.

assertions.text: Treats published as optional
Routes to references/gotchas.md or references/api.md

evals.name: empty-query-500
evals.prompt: Synthetic search returns a blank 500 when my script sends query: "". Is it free to retry?
evals.expected_output: Explains empty queries return a blank 500 that still costs hourly search quota, recommends validating non-blank queries locally, and notes missing or non-string query returns a free 400.

assertions.text: States the blank 500 still counts against the hourly search quota
Recommends local validation before sending

evals.name: irrelevant-results
evals.prompt: I searched Synthetic for an obscure internal codename and got 5 results that look unrelated. Did it find anything?
evals.expected_output: Explains the API always returns 5 results even when nothing matches, so the results should be judged for relevance and likely mean no real match; suggests refining or narrowing the query.

assertions.text: States that Synthetic never returns an empty result set

evals.name: url-lookup
evals.prompt: Use Synthetic to grab the content of https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/.
evals.expected_output: Uses the URL as the query, checks that result 1 matches the URL, reads its text from a saved response, and explains this works only for indexed pages and is not a live fetch.

assertions.text: Verifies result 1 is the requested URL before using its text
Explains URL queries are index lookups rather than live fetches

evals.name: structured-probe
evals.prompt: Synthetic search seems to behave differently from the skill. Re-verify the limits in a machine-readable way.
evals.expected_output: Runs python3 scripts/probe_synthetic_search.py --mode limits (and optionally errors/quotas), compares output to references/evidence.md, and proposes a sourced correction rather than silently editing the installed skill.

assertions.text: Uses the probe script and states its quota cost
Compares against references/evidence.md

evals.name: raw-curl-without-node
evals.prompt: Node isn't installed. Give me a curl command for Synthetic search that won't flood my terminal.
evals.expected_output: Gives a curl POST to https://api.synthetic.new/v2/search with the Bearer header and a jq-built JSON body, piped to a jq projection of title, url, published, and a trimmed highlight.

assertions.text: Uses POST https://api.synthetic.new/v2/search with Authorization: Bearer
Projects away the full text field with jq

evals.name: negative-other-search-provider
evals.prompt: Use Tavily to search for recent AI startup funding rounds.
evals.expected_output: Does not trigger synthetic-search because the user explicitly asked for Tavily.

assertions.text: Does not route to synthetic-search when another provider is requested

evals.name: negative-browser-automation
evals.prompt: Open this site, click around the navigation, and capture a screenshot of the pricing tab.
evals.expected_output: Does not trigger synthetic-search because the task is browser automation.

assertions.text: Does not route to synthetic-search for browser automation
